subject: Post-demo: TTFT & streaming delivery checklist for FinServe pilot
messages:
From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@finservelabs.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Daria Petrov <daria.petrov@finservelabs.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: TTFT & streaming delivery checklist for FinServe pilot

Camila — thanks for the demo this morning. High level, that looks promising. A few clarifying items from our side so we can map to our procurement and infra teams: 

1) Time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectations: we need a working target and a stretch target. For the pilot we'll require a 95th percentile TTFT of <= 180ms under our steady-state traffic (concurrency = 50), and a stretch goal of <= 120ms if we move to Dedicated. Cold-starts during autoscale are a real concern; we need documented behavior there.

2) Streaming interface: our product team prefers SSE (server-sent events) for the first phase (web clients), but we have a subset of mobile clients that need WebSocket fallbacks. Any differences in token cadence / chunk sizes between SSE and WS that we should be aware of?

3) Chunk cadence for UX: target is to show partial tokens every ~300–500ms for long-form responses; if the model emits sparse bursts, we want a predictable buffering policy so the frontend doesn't freeze.

4) Throughput & bursts: steady throughput for pilot estimated at 1,000 reqs/day with concurrency peaks to 200 for short windows. We need guidance on autoscale and cost trade-offs.

Can you share a simple acceptance test plan we can run during the POC (scripts or steps) and any sample metrics to look for (TTFT histogram, chunk latency, token yield per second)?

If possible, please include a rough timeline for a pilot (1–2 weeks test window preferred).

Thanks — Alex
Senior PM, FinServe Labs

Subject: Re: Post-demo: TTFT & streaming delivery checklist for FinServe pilot

Alex / Daria — thanks again for the call. Per our discussion, attached is a lightweight POC checklist and an initial benchmark plan (ttft-benchmark-plan.xlsx) that we can run together. Highlights below — putting concrete numbers against your asks so engineering can triage.

Quick summary (engineer's view):
- Working TTFT target (95th pctl): 180ms under 50 concurrent steady sessions.
- Stretch TTFT target: 120ms under Dedicated profile + quantized model.
- Cold-start guardrail: < 1s median, dependent on reserved pools. We'll document fallback behavior (serve from warm pool / scaled-down model variant).
- Streaming transport: SSE first phase; WebSocket supported for mobile clients. No functional differences in tokenization; differences are in connection semantics and browser reconnection.
- Chunk cadence recommendations: 200–400ms target cadence for human-typing feel. If model emits tokens faster, continuous streaming will push smaller chunks more frequently; if the model stalls, add a heartbeat chunk at 300ms to avoid UI stalls.
- Concurrency & bursting: recommend reserved capacity for 200 peak burst windows; autoscale cold-starts cost/time trade-offs documented in attachment.

Next steps / asks for FinServe (mutual action plan):
1) Your infra contact to provide a small public test harness (URL + auth) we can hit for TTFT/streaming tests.
2) Confirm whether SSE-only is acceptable for web (Y/N) and list mobile client count for WS fallback.
3) Approve the test window (we propose 7 business days starting when both sides are ready).
4) Provide any compliance artifacts required for Private deployment evaluation (if you want us to scope VPC/on-prem).

I've included a quick acceptance checklist in the attached markdown (streaming-cadence-proposal.md) and a measured micro-benchmark we ran this morning (arch-drawings.png plus numbers in the spreadsheet).

If helpful, I'll have Karthik jump on a short call tomorrow to walk through the engineering checklist and run a live TTFT measurement.

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: TTFT & streaming delivery checklist for FinServe pilot

Camila — this is great, thanks. A few clarifications from Eng Ops after reading the plan: 

• Cold-start SLA: 1s median is acceptable, but we need a documented remediation if cold-start exceeds 2s consistently (alerts + temporary routing to lighter model).
• TTFT under load: our internal SLA will be 99th pctl <= 300ms for the pilot; since you propose 95th @180ms we'll use your bench to validate. Need the bench script.
• SSE vs WebSocket: SSE fine for web. For mobile, we require WS fallback with automatic reconnection within 2s and explicit chunk-reassembly guidance for partial tokens (we'll align on protobuf vs newline-delimited JSON).

Also, we can spin up the test harness by Monday. For the pilot scope: we'll start with a static dataset of prompts (50 prompts of mixed length) and run concurrency sweeps (10, 25, 50, 100) across three runs each. Will that map to your bench?

Daria
Eng Ops, FinServe Labs

Hi Daria / Alex — Karthik here (runtime engineering). Quick answers and what I'll bring to the pilot bench call:

1) Bench scripts: attaching a small harness (see Drive link) that performs: warm run (populate KV cache), steady-state run (concurrency sweep), and cold-start measurement (spin up from zero). It reports TTFT histogram, per-chunk latency distribution, and token throughput. We'll hand over a runnable Docker container for your infra team.

2) Cold-start remediation: we'll implement an alert when 95th pctl TTFT > 1s for 5 minutes; automatic fallback is to route to a low-latency quantized variant until warm pool recovers. We'll provide the config snippet for canary routing.

3) SSE vs WS payloads: payloads are identical (newline-delimited JSON chunks). For mobile WS, we'll recommend a compact protobuf-encoded chunk for bandwidth-savings; we'll include encoding examples in the repo. Chunk reassembly logic: simple sequence-id + final_flag boolean — I'll add an example in the harness.

4) Cadence tuning: we'll expose a server-side max_hold_ms parameter (default 300ms) which forces a heartbeat chunk if no tokens are emitted; this should satisfy the UI cadence needs.

I'll join the pilot kickoff on Monday and walk through the Docker harness and metrics dashboard. If you can grant our engineering GitHub org access to the test harness repo, I will drop the runbook and the scripts ahead of time.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
